verdict.rationale: Meltano's own CLI covers the main pipeline lifecycle. `meltano init` scaffolds a project, `meltano add` installs plugins idempotently, `meltano config list` and `meltano config test` inspect and validate settings, and `meltano run` executes EL(T) pipelines. A CLI-first tool like this is usable by a coding agent without a UI. Coverage is still not complete: the evidence never shows a non-interactive command that sets config values, nothing documents agent-oriented or headless use, and there is no API (llms.txt and OpenAPI probes returned 404). Missing for 10: a documented non-interactive config-setting command, documentation or hands-on corroboration of agent or headless use, and an API surface or agent-friendly docs such as llms.txt.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, a coding agent can scaffold, configure, and run a complete pipeline headlessly through the CLI or API

citations.quote: Initialize a new project in a directory of your choosing using meltano init
`meltano add` lets you add or update [plugins](/concepts/plugins#project-plugins) in your Meltano project. The command is idempotent
meltano config list <plugin> to list all available settings with their names, environment variables, and current values.
You can run EL(T) pipelines using [`meltano run`]
Meltano provides a command line interface (CLI) that makes it easy to manage your project, plugins, and EL(T) pipelines.
